title: Longest Path
explanation: Longest path is NP-hard in general but easy on a DAG: process vertices in topological order (or memoized DFS).
traps: Running Dijkstra with negated weights is wrong (negative edges).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[v] = length of the longest path starting at v
dp[mask][v] = longest path visiting exactly the set mask ending at v
options.why: That's for general graphs (Hamiltonian-style); a DAG doesn't need it, and N = 1e5.

options.text: dp[k] = whether a path of length k exists

options.why: Asks for the longest path over all starts, not a shortest path.

options.text: dp[v] = length of the longest path ending at v

extraLayers.explanation: Because there are no cycles, the best path from v only depends on the best paths from its out-neighbours. (Ending at v works too.)

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[v] = max over edges v→u of dp[u] + 1, computed in reverse topological order (or memoized DFS)
dp[v] = max over edges v→u of dp[u] + 1, computed in increasing vertex index
options.why: Vertex numbers aren't a topological order.

options.text: Relax edges with a priority queue keyed by −length

extraLayers.explanation: Evaluate a vertex only after all its successors — exactly what topological order guarantees.
